name: Client Brief — Orientation Happy Path
query: I've got a call with the Bradys in ten minutes
expected_behavior: Step 1: Calls Wealth:find_client with the name the advisor used — not Wealth:get_clients alone
Step 2: Finds two matching households (Brady/CA and Brady-Hollis/TX) and asks which, as a table
Step 3: The disambiguation table has exactly the columns Client, Family name, State, Spouse
Step 4: On the advisor naming California, calls Wealth:find_client again with that wid (resolution DIRECT) and Wealth:list_documents
Step 5: Presents the profile from the DIRECT result without a second profile call
Step 6: States the children indicator without naming any child
Step 7: Presents the document table with exactly the columns Document, Type, Upload date, Document date
Step 8: Names the Fidelity statement as non-estate rather than omitting it
Step 9: Offers exactly one next step, phrased as a question, naming a document
success_criteria: Client is named in the first sentence of the substantive answer
Zero identifiers (wid, vaultId) in the answer text
The children/spouse fact is stated as an indicator, never as a name
Exactly one offer, phrased as a question
Tool sequence is Wealth:find_client (2x total: once to search, once DIRECT by wid) then Wealth:list_documents (1x)

Zero calls to get_client_info, get_contact_cards, get_estate_roles, get_estate_flow, or get_flowchart — none exist or none apply here (get_flowchart requires a vaultId, so it has no household-level use)
must_not: any email, phone number, street address, date of birth, or account identifier in the disambiguation table
any tool name, field path, or internal label in advisor-facing text
a child's or spouse's name produced from anywhere
a Status column on the document table
a table with a single row
proceeding with either Brady household without the advisor choosing
